title: 90833 CPT Code: Time Range, E/M Pairing, and Documentation
summary: The 90833 CPT code is the add-on for 16 to 37 minutes of psychotherapy with an E/M service. Time range, why it is never billed alone, and what to document.
body_markdown:
**The 90833 CPT code covers 16 to 37 minutes of psychotherapy delivered during the same encounter as an evaluation and management service.** It is an add-on code, which means it is reported alongside an E/M code and never on its own.


The official CPT descriptor reads "Psychotherapy, 30 minutes with patient when performed with an evaluation and management service," while the billable range runs from 16 to 37 minutes. The descriptor names the typical session; the range decides the claim.


90833 is the code prescribers reach for most often and get wrong most often. It applies to the visit that was part medication management and part therapy: you adjust a treatment plan, then spend real time working through what the patient brought in. The two failures are billing[90832](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/90832-cpt-code) when an add-on was required, and letting 90833 reach a claim without the E/M service it attaches to.


## The 90833 CPT Code Time Range


The three psychotherapy add-on codes are timed, and each billable range is set by the midpoint rule rather than by the number in the descriptor. A session qualifies for a code once it passes the midpoint between that code and the one below it.


Add-on code Documented psychotherapy time Standalone equivalent


**90833** **16 to 37 minutes** 90832


90836 38 to 52 minutes 90834


90838 53 minutes or more 90837


Those ranges are the ones CMS applies: choose the code closest to the actual time,[16 to 37 minutes for 90832 and 90833, 38 to 52 for 90834 and 90836, and 53 or more for 90837 and 90838](https://www.cms.gov/medicare-coverage-database/view/article.aspx?articleId=57520) .


It is worth stating plainly what these codes are **not** , because the misconception is common: none of them is a telehealth code. 90836 is not "the telehealth one". It is the 38 to 52 minute tier. Telehealth is conveyed by place of service and, where required, a modifier, never by choosing a different add-on code.


### What Counts Toward the Psychotherapy Time


Only the time spent delivering psychotherapy counts, and it has to be time that is not also supporting the E/M service. The evaluation and management portion is selected on medical decision making rather than on time, precisely because the time is being used elsewhere. Minutes cannot be counted twice.


The psychotherapy time does not have to be one unbroken block. CMS recognises that "the psychotherapy time may not be continuous in a combined psychotherapy with an E/M service", so therapy delivered either side of the medical portion of the visit still counts, provided the total is documented and kept separate from the E/M work.


Below 16 minutes of psychotherapy, no add-on applies. The encounter is an E/M service alone, and adding 90833 to it because some therapeutic conversation took place is the kind of pattern that looks deliberate in aggregate even when each instance was well intentioned.


## Can You Bill 99214 and 90833 Together?


**Yes.** This is the pairing 90833 exists for. 99214 is an office or outpatient evaluation and management code, 90833 is the psychotherapy add-on that attaches to it, and the two are billed together on a single encounter whenever both services were genuinely delivered.


Add-on codes have no standalone value, so 90833 has to attach to something. In practice that is the E/M service the prescriber is already reporting for the visit, most commonly the office and outpatient codes in the 99202 to 99215 range. The add-ons also travel with E/M services in other settings, and the full set your plan recognises is set out in the CMS[Billing and Coding: Psychiatry and Psychology Services](https://www.cms.gov/medicare-coverage-database/view/article.aspx?articleId=57480) article. That guidance is the floor rather than the ceiling: commercial plans layer on their own requirements and they differ from each other, so confirm the pairing per payer rather than carrying forward last year's configuration.


Two conditions decide whether the pair survives review. The psychotherapy must reach 16 minutes, and the psychotherapy time must be documented separately from the time and work supporting the E/M service. The E/M level is selected on medical decision making, and any time counted toward psychotherapy cannot also support the E/M level.


What you cannot do is bill 99214 with 90832. When psychotherapy is delivered inside an E/M encounter, the add-on is required and the standalone code is wrong. Our[guide to psychiatric billing](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/the-complete-guide-to-psychiatric-billing-from-e-m-to-psychotherapy-with-ai-powered-support) covers how the two families sit together across a full practice.


## Which Providers Can Bill 90833, and Where Payers Differ


Because 90833 attaches to an evaluation and management service, it can only be reported by a clinician who is reporting that E/M service. CMS describes the pairing as psychotherapy performed with an E/M "by the same physician or NPP", and lists the practitioners who may furnish these services as physicians and non-physician practitioners including nurse practitioners, clinical nurse specialists and physician assistants, in each case only where the service falls within the scope of their state licence and clinical practice.


This is the sharpest difference between 90833 and 90832. A clinician who cannot report an evaluation and management service cannot report the add-on that attaches to one, so a therapist, clinical social worker, counselor or marriage and family therapist bills[90832](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/90832-cpt-code) for a short session instead: psychotherapy is the whole encounter, and there is no E/M service for an add-on to attach to.


Scope of practice and payer recognition are also two different things. A licence that permits a service in your state does not guarantee every plan credentials that licence type for it, and Medicaid programmes vary state by state on which practitioners may bill directly rather than under supervision. Where a supervising provider is required, confirm which NPI belongs on the claim, because a correctly coded 90833 still denies under the wrong rendering provider.


## 90833 vs 90832: Which One to Bill


These two are not alternatives you choose between on clinical grounds. They describe the same amount of psychotherapy in two different billing situations.


90832 is what you bill when psychotherapy is the whole encounter. 90833 is what you bill alongside an E/M code when psychotherapy happened during a medical visit. Same 16 to 37 minute range, mutually exclusive on a single encounter. If you find both on one claim line for one visit, something is wrong.


Practices with both prescribers and therapists on staff tend to get this wrong in exactly one place: the prescribers' claims.


## Add-On Codes and Modifiers That Travel With 90833


**Interactive complexity (90785)** applies when specific communication factors complicate the session, such as involving a third party, managing a caregiver conflict that interferes with treatment, or working through an interpreter. It is not a marker for a difficult session and it is not a way to account for extra time.


**Telehealth** is reported with the place of service reflecting where the patient was, commonly 02 for telehealth outside the home and 10 for telehealth in the home, and modifier 95 where the payer requires it. These requirements have been revised more than once and differ between Medicare and commercial plans, so confirm the current expectation per payer.


**Prolonged services cannot be reported here.** CMS is explicit: "Time may not be used as the basis of E/M code selection and prolonged services may not be reported when psychotherapy with E/M (90833, 90836, 90838) are reported." Psychotherapy that runs past 37 minutes simply becomes 90836. If a coding reference or internal cheat sheet in your practice still pairs psychotherapy with the retired prolonged service codes 99354 and 99355, it is describing a rule that no longer applies.


## What 90833 Pays and How to Look Up Your Rate


There is no single national figure worth quoting. Medicare rates are set by the Physician Fee Schedule and adjusted by geographic locality, so the same code pays differently in different metropolitan areas, and commercial rates come from your individual contracts. Any article giving you one number for 90833 is giving you an average that does not describe your practice.


The add-on is also paid on top of the E/M service rather than instead of it, so the comparison that matters is the E/M alone against the E/M plus 90833, using your own contracted rates. That difference, multiplied by the number of medication visits per month that genuinely included 16 minutes or more of psychotherapy, is what missing the add-on costs you.


For the Medicare figure that applies to you, use the[CMS Physician Fee Schedule Look-Up Tool](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/physician-fee-schedule/search) with your locality and the current year. The official code definition is maintained by the[AAPC code reference](https://www.aapc.com/codes/cpt-codes/90833) , and[APA Services](https://www.apaservices.org/practice/reimbursement/health-codes/psychotherapy) maintains practical guidance on the psychotherapy code set.


## Common 90833 Billing Mistakes


Six errors account for most 90833 denials and most of the revenue quietly left behind:


- **Billing 90832 instead of 90833.** The prescriber delivered psychotherapy inside a medication visit and reached for the standalone code. This is the single most common error in the code.
- **Sending 90833 without a primary E/M code.** An add-on with nothing to attach to denies every time.
- **Recording one block of time for the whole visit.** Nothing in that note establishes how much of the encounter was psychotherapy, so the add-on is the part that falls away under review.
- **Selecting the E/M level on time.** When psychotherapy is also billed, the E/M is selected on medical decision making. The same minutes cannot support both.
- **Treating 90836 as the telehealth code.** It is the 38 to 52 minute tier. Telehealth is conveyed by place of service and modifier.
- **Pairing psychotherapy with 99354.** That code was deleted effective 1 January 2023 and was not replaced for psychotherapy.


Only the first two produce a denial you will notice. The rest either pay cleanly at the wrong amount or fail later under review, which is why 90833 problems tend to surface as an audit rather than as a rejection.


## Documentation Checklist for a 90833 Session


A 90833 note that holds up under review records the following:


- Elapsed psychotherapy time, or start and stop times, confirming it reached 16 minutes
- That the psychotherapy time is separate from the time and work supporting the E/M service
- The psychotherapeutic modality used
- The presenting problem and current status
- The intervention delivered in this session, specific enough to distinguish it from the last one
- The patient's response
- The medical decision making supporting the E/M level
- The plan, including the reason for the next contact
- The service modality, in person or telehealth, and the patient's location if telehealth
- A signature and credentials matching the rendering provider on the claim


### Why the Two Time Records Have to Be Separate


A single note that records one block of time for the whole visit cannot support 90833, because nothing in it establishes how much of that time was psychotherapy. Under review the add-on is the part that falls away, and the encounter pays as an E/M service alone.


Start and stop times for the psychotherapy portion are the most frequently omitted element, and their absence is what turns an arguable claim into an indefensible one. Our[note structure guide](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/soap-note-example) covers the format, and[behavioral health billing](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/behavioral-health-billing) covers where these fields land on the claim.


## Where the Coding Decision Should Live


90833 depends on two facts that are accurate the moment the encounter ends and steadily less accurate afterwards: how long the psychotherapy ran, and where it sat inside a visit that was also an E/M service. A clinician writing notes at the end of a clinic day is reconstructing both, and reconstruction compresses toward the schedule.


A practice billing 90833 correctly is one where the split is captured while it is still a fact rather than reassembled later. That is a workflow question rather than a coding question, and it is where[billing software built for behavioral health](https://www.mdhub.ai/use-cases/mental-health-billing-software) earns its place: the time, the modality and the code reach the claim from the session itself, and the clinician confirms rather than remembers.

Accurate 90833 billing comes down to whether the psychotherapy time was separated from the E/M work while both were still facts. Can CPT code 99214 and 90833 be billed together?


Yes. 99214 is an office or outpatient evaluation and management code and 90833 is the psychotherapy add-on that attaches to it, so the pair is valid on a single encounter when both services were genuinely delivered. Two conditions apply. The psychotherapy must run at least 16 minutes, and that time must be documented separately from the time and work supporting the E/M service. The E/M level is then selected on medical decision making rather than on time, because the time is already being used for the psychotherapy. What you cannot do is bill 99214 with 90832: when psychotherapy happens inside an E/M encounter the add-on is required, not the standalone code.


What is the difference between 90832 and 90833?


The billing situation, not the amount of therapy. Both cover 16 to 37 minutes of psychotherapy. 90832 is what you bill when psychotherapy is the entire encounter. 90833 is an add-on billed alongside an evaluation and management code when psychotherapy happened during a medical visit, and it can never be billed alone. The two are mutually exclusive on a single encounter, so if you find both on one claim line for one visit, something is wrong. The practical consequence is that they are usually billed by different people: 90832 by therapists, 90833 by prescribers.


Can CPT 90833 be billed alone?


No. Add-on codes have no standalone value, so 90833 will deny if it reaches a claim without the E/M service it attaches to. If psychotherapy was the entire encounter and no E/M service was performed, the correct code is the standalone one for the documented time: 90832 for 16 to 37 minutes, 90834 for 38 to 52, 90837 for 53 or more.


How much does a 90833 pay?


There is no single national figure worth quoting. Medicare rates are set by the Physician Fee Schedule and adjusted by geographic locality, so the same code pays differently in different metropolitan areas, and commercial rates come from your individual contracts. Because 90833 is an add-on it is paid on top of the E/M service rather than instead of it, so the comparison that matters to your practice is the E/M alone against the E/M plus 90833 at your own contracted rates. For the Medicare figure that applies to you, use the CMS Physician Fee Schedule Look-Up Tool with your locality and the current year.
